name: Meridian
tagline: Quiet surfaces. One blue. Nothing to forgive.

tokens.name: canvas
tokens.usage: Page ground. Visibly a step below the surfaces by day; true near-black by night.

tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: Cards, fields, menus, the rail. Separated from canvas by a hairline and a 1px top highlight, never a drop shadow.

tokens.name: surface-sunk
tokens.usage: Code wells, table header, inactive tracks, the inside of a keyboard key, the row hover tint.

tokens.name: hairline
tokens.usage: Every border. One weight, one colour, everywhere.

tokens.name: hairline-strong
tokens.usage: Borders on hover, the active field, the table header rule, the top of a glass card.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Primary text and icons.

tokens.name: ink-soft
tokens.usage: Secondary text, labels, placeholders, captions.

tokens.name: ink-faint
tokens.usage: Tertiary text: timestamps, helper text, disabled labels, the drawing line.

tokens.name: blue
tokens.usage: The one colour. Primary actions, links, the focus ring, the first series. One fill per view.

tokens.name: on-blue
tokens.usage: Text and icons on blue fills.

tokens.name: blue-soft
tokens.usage: Tinted ground for the active nav item, selected rows, info callouts.

tokens.name: blue-ink
tokens.usage: Blue as text: links, the active nav label, the selected tab.

tokens.name: positive
tokens.usage: Success text and the up-delta. Always paired with a word or a dot.

tokens.name: positive-soft
tokens.usage: Ground for success tags.

tokens.name: caution
tokens.usage: Warnings and pending states.

tokens.name: caution-soft
tokens.usage: Ground for warning tags.

tokens.name: negative
tokens.usage: Errors, destructive actions, the down-delta.

tokens.name: negative-soft
tokens.usage: Ground for error tags and callouts.

tokens.name: violet
tokens.usage: Second chart series only.

tokens.name: teal
tokens.usage: Third chart series only.

type_roles.name: display-xl
type_roles.usage: One per page. Hero headlines. Semibold, never bold: the presence comes from size and tracking, not weight.

type_roles.name: title
type_roles.usage: Card titles, dialog titles, table group heads.

type_roles.name: body-l
type_roles.sample: Meridian keeps the surface quiet so the one thing that matters can be loud.

type_roles.name: body
type_roles.sample: Invoices are issued on the first of the month and settle within three days.
type_roles.usage: Default UI and reading text. 14px: product density, not a blog.

type_roles.name: label
type_roles.usage: Field labels, column heads, stat labels. Medium weight, sentence case: Meridian never shouts.

type_roles.name: eyebrow
type_roles.usage: Section eyebrows and breadcrumbs in the mono, with a dot. The only place the mono appears outside code.

type_roles.name: numeral
type_roles.usage: KPI figures in the sans, tabular, with the unit set smaller beside them. Mono is for code, not for money.

idea_headline: The product that gets out of the way.
idea: Meridian is the look of software confident enough to be quiet: a grey canvas, white surfaces that sit on it under a 1px top highlight, hairlines instead of shadows, 14px sans everywhere, and one blue used exactly once per view. At night the surfaces turn to glass with a gradient edge and a soft blue glow behind the hero. Nothing decorates; depth comes from layering, hierarchy from spacing and tracking, and the only coloured things are the data and the one action.
use_for: Product dashboards, settings and billing screens, developer and product docs, SaaS marketing pages, changelogs, anything a professional reads every day and should never notice the chrome of.
avoid_when: Editorial or narrative subjects, anything that wants warmth, print or texture, consumer brands with a personality to show, or a page whose job is to be remembered rather than used.
principles: The page is a grey canvas; everything that holds content is a white surface on it, with a hairline and a 1px top highlight so it sits rather than floats. A shadow means the thing is floating: a palette, a menu, a toast.
Blue is the primary action, the link, the active nav item and the focus ring. In any one view only one element is a blue fill.
14px body, 22px leading, 8px steps. A professional reads this all day; give them the information, not the air.
Display type is semibold with negative tracking that tightens as it grows. Bold is never used.
The chrome has no colour. Charts, status dots and deltas are the only coloured things, so they are the first things seen.
voice: Short, literal, present tense: "Invoice sent." "3 seats remaining."
Sentence case everywhere, including buttons and column heads.
Numbers carry the message; the sentence around them is as short as it can be.
Keyboard shortcuts are shown, not described: ⌘K, not "press command and K".
colour_headline: Two greys, one white, one blue.
colour_note: Day is a grey canvas with white surfaces; Night is near-black with surfaces one step lighter and a gradient edge. The hairline is the only structural colour. Blue carries action and focus; three status colours carry state and always come with a dot or a word. Violet and teal exist only for charts.
chart_note: Blue is the focal series; violet and teal exist only for charts so they never compete with action or status. The fourth series is grey. Gridlines are the hairline; the axis line is removed.
type_note: One family for display and UI, semibold above 28px with tracking tightening as size grows; regular 400 for everything readable. Geist Mono carries code, keys, and the dotted eyebrow. Labels are medium weight in sentence case: there is no caps role in Meridian.
space_headline: An 8px grid, a 1px line, an 8px corner.
space: Gaps between an icon and its label; tag padding-y.
Gaps inside controls; between stacked fields.
Card padding on dense screens; gap between cards.
Card padding on wide screens; section padding inside a page.
edges: Tags, keyboard keys, inline code chips, small buttons.
Buttons, fields, cards, menus. The default.
Dialogs, the command palette, the marketing hero card.
Every border. Strengthens to hairline-strong on hover and on the active field.
depth: A 1px top highlight and a 2% contact shadow on every surface: cards sit on the canvas. Never a drop shadow on a tile.
The command palette, menus, dialogs and toasts: a 1px contact line plus a 40px drop at 22%. The only real shadow.
At night a card is a surface with a gradient edge from hairline-strong to nothing, so the top catches light.
A radial blue glow behind a hero or an empty state, 10% by day and 18% at night. The only gradient besides glass.
Keyboard keys have a 2px inset bottom and a 1px drop, like a real keycap.
A 2px canvas gap then 2px blue. On every control, never removed.
motion: Borders strengthen and surfaces tint by one step, 120ms ease-out. Nothing moves on hover except a link underline.
Buttons scale to 0.98 for 80ms. No colour change beyond the hover tint.
The kit reveal-up at 240ms with 60ms stagger for card grids. One pass on page load; nothing re-animates on scroll.
The palette and menus fade and rise 4px in 160ms; they leave in 100ms.
One: the live status dot pulses every 2.4s. A spinner is the only other thing that moves on its own.
Lines draw in over 400ms on first paint; bars grow from the baseline. Reduced motion shows the finished chart.
components_headline: The kit already looks like this.
components_note: Meridian is close to the contract's native shape, so kit components arrive nearly finished: white surfaces, hairlines, 8px corners, a blue primary. The authored classes add the top highlight, the keycap, the status dot, the glass edge and the command palette.

tags_note: Status tags are a 6px dot plus a word in sentence case on a soft ground. The dot is the colour; the word is the meaning. A live dot pulses.
fields_note: Fields are white surfaces with a hairline; the label sits above in the label role and helper text below in ink-faint. Focus swaps the hairline for the blue ring.

stats_note: A stat is a label, a sans numeral and a delta. Stats share one card and are separated by hairlines, never boxed individually. The delta is the only coloured text.
callouts:

Invoices settle in 3 days. Payouts arrive the following business day.

callouts_note: A callout is a hairline box with a 2px left rule in the status colour. The ground stays white except for errors, which take the soft red.
chart_comp_note: Charts take blue first and violet second with no area fills. Gridlines are the hairline; the axis line is removed; labels are ink-soft at 12px.
table_note: Tables are the densest thing in Meridian: 12px padding, hairline rows, a sunk header with a hairline-strong rule, tabular figures right-aligned, initials avatars beside names. No zebra stripes; hover tints the row by one step.

motifs_headline: Hairlines, keys, a palette, and a 1.5px line.
motifs_note: Meridian's devices are the furniture of good software: the command palette, the keycap, the status dot, the glass edge, the shine divider and the metric row. Each is a hairline, a surface and at most one blue.

dos: Put every surface on the canvas with a hairline and the 1px top highlight; reserve the shadow for things that float.
Sentence case everywhere, including buttons and table heads.
Keep body at 14px and let spacing make the hierarchy.
Show shortcuts as keycaps beside the action they trigger.
donts: No bold display type; semibold with tight tracking is the ceiling.
No caps labels, no letter-spaced eyebrows; the mono eyebrow with a dot is the only ornament.
No gradients beyond the glow and the glass edge, no coloured chrome.
No rounded corners above 12px; Meridian is not friendly, it is calm.
binding_losses: The top highlight, the glass edge, the glow, the keycap inset and the hairline-strong hover state have no contract slot; they are the --ds-* properties and me-* classes above. Kit components already match the shape of Meridian, so the losses are small.

hand.headline: Thin grey lines, one blue shape, nothing filled.
hand.note: Meridian draws the way its docs draw: 1.5px lines in the faint ink with round caps, surfaces left white, exactly one shape in blue and the second role as a blue outline. No shadows, no texture, no hatching; the drawing should look like a figure from a well-made API reference.
rules: 1.5px in ink-faint, round caps and joins. The drawing is quieter than the text around it.
None, except the one blue shape per drawing. The secondary role is a blue outline at 40%.
None. A drawing sits on the surface like a diagram.

tpl.slide_body: Existing customers grew their spend faster than churn removed it. Above 100 is expansion; this quarter it is the highest on record.
tpl.ed_headline: Invoices now settle in three days
tpl.ed_deck: Payouts used to wait for the end of the week. From this release they clear on the third business day, and the billing page shows the exact date.
tpl.ed_byline: By the billing team · 2 Oct 2026 · 3 min read
tpl.ed_body: Settlement used to be the slowest part of getting paid. An invoice marked paid on Monday would not reach a bank account until the following Monday, and nothing on the billing page said so. From today the settlement window is three business days, the payout date is printed on every paid invoice, and a webhook fires the moment the transfer leaves.
steps: Each square is one workspace. Sixty start on Team, twenty-five on Starter, fifteen on a trial.
The trials have decided: most converted to Team. The grey squares are the ones that left.
tpl.step_caption: Fig. 1 · One cohort of 100 workspaces, by plan · synthetic
tpl.landing_sub: Usage-based billing, dunning and payouts in one quiet dashboard. Set up in an afternoon; never think about it again.
features: Meter any event and bill it monthly, with proration handled for you.
Retry schedules, card-update emails and a hosted portal, on by default.
Settled funds reach your account on the third business day, every time.
tpl.plan_title: Usage-based billing: from meter to invoice
tpl.plan_outcome: A workspace can meter any event, see the running bill on S1 before the month closes, and receive a correct invoice on S2 with no manual adjustment.
tpl.plan_scope: Meter ingestion, the running-bill screen (S1), the invoice preview (S2) and the parse-error recovery (S2e). Out: proration rules, credits, multi-currency.
tpl.plan_status: Plan only · 2 of 6 tasks done · parser verified on fixtures, nothing in production
tpl.plan_screens_note: S1 desktop keeps the rail and the stat row beside the usage chart; S1 mobile stacks the running bill above the metered rows and moves "Preview invoice" to a bottom action.
tpl.plan_flow:
flowchart LR
  A((Meter events)) -->|Ingest| B[S1 Running bill]
  B -->|Preview invoice| C{Lines reconcile?}
  C -->|Yes| D[S2 Invoice preview]
  C -->|No| E[S2e Unmatched meters]
  E -->|Map and retry| C
  D -->|Issue| F((Invoice sent))
plan_decisions: Show the bill before it is a bill.
S1 is the running total, updated as events land, so the invoice on S2 is never a surprise.
Preview invoice on S1, Issue on S2. Everything else is a link or a ⌘K command.
Unmatched meters block issue, not ingest.
Events are always accepted; S2e lists the meters with no price and keeps the mapping the user has done.
plan_tasks: Meter ingestion idempotent on event id
S1 running-bill query under 200ms at 1M events
Verify a full month on the fixture workspace
tpl.plan_acceptance: Done means: a fixture workspace with one million events shows the right running bill on S1 within 200ms and issues the matching invoice from S2, and an unmatched meter routes through S2e without losing the mapping.
